item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated local socket): "Implement `retry_budget.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: make retry_budget.py match SPEC.md exactly. Read SPEC.md in the repository root first and treat it as the contract.
Acceptance criteria:
- Every public name and signature documented in SPEC.md is preserved or implemented as specified.
- Every error case and boundary case in SPEC.md is handled as specified, with the specified exception types and messages.
- Add focused tests covering the spec's error and boundary cases, in addition to the existing basic tests. Existing tests must still pass.
- Standard library only; no new dependencies.
- Keep functions under 60 lines, validate inputs at the boundary, and never swallow exceptions.
- Commit the work in the repository's local branch with a clear message. Use the repository's configured git identity. Do not add AI or tool attribution lines (no Co-Authored-By, no "generated by" text) to commit messages.
- If SPEC.md is missing or ambiguous on a point that changes behaviour, pick the most reasonable reading, state it in the commit body, and report it in the summary.

state.summary:
Implemented retry_delay in retry_budget.py per SPEC.md and added focused tests. Committed as ddcbf8f on archon/thd7zqmj-implement-retry-budget-py-per-spec-md (tree 2fabf1f52bfced266e3815b255445d46df0140f2); not pushed. Before: the stub raised NotImplementedError and all 3 existing tests errored. After: 28 tests pass under `python3 -W error -m unittest -v`. The implementation is stdlib-only and validates all arguments before any early return. It rejects non-built-in-int values (bool, float, int subclasses) and out-of-range values with ValueError. Backoff saturates without building a large power. Retry-After is an uncapped floor, and the budget check is strict. Interpretation choices, recorded in the commit body: wrong-type inputs raise ValueError (per the spec's "invalid values raise ValueError", not TypeError), and the messages are my own. pr.body: Files: retry_budget.py (retry_delay, _require_int, _backoff), test_retry_budget.py (existing basics kept; new classes for validation, attempt limit, backoff bounds, Retry-After floor, budget boundaries). Approach: validate all args first; attempt >= max_attempts returns None; backoff = min(cap, base << (attempt-1)) with a bit_length shortcut so huge attempts never build a large power; delay = max(backoff, retry_after) when supplied; return None when elapsed + delay >= budget, else delay. Checks: py_compile clean under -W error; unittest 28/28 OK under -W error. Assumptions: wrong-type args raise ValueError as the spec states; no TypeError. Limits: no linter available in the environment (pyflakes/flake8 not installed), so only compile and line-length checks were run. Follow-ups: none.
pr.summary: made retry_delay() real: exponential backoff capped at cap_ms, Retry-After floor, strict budget check. now validates inputs and returns None or a delay per spec. before: stub raised NotImplementedError; now: 28 tests pass.
